rail_guard.text: Bushmills Station, home of the little steam railway to the Causeway. Narrow gauge, big smile, and a chimney that thinks it's a volcano.
Hop aboard. The Wildlore rail runs to any town you have visited on this island. Where to?

then.text: Rain's good for the Bush. The wheel spins faster and looks very pleased with itself.
Wind like this, the wheel thinks it's a windmill. Don't tell it otherwise.

mill_keeper.text: Don't tell anyone, but the mill hasn't ground a grain in a century. The wheel still turns, though, for the tourists. It likes the audience.
The Bush is a quick little river. Quick to flood, quick to clear. Like a Bushmills argument.

then.text: There's a bittern booming on the Bush. A bittern! My Sammy says it's a foghorn. My Sammy's an eejit.
Sun on the tulips! They're showing off now. You can't tell them anything.
Up with the birds. They supervise, I dig. It's a fair arrangement.

else.text: I do the flower beds on the green. Two hundred years of Bushmills folk have walked across them, and not one asked permission.
Planting tulips is an act of faith. You bury a thing in the cold, in the dark, and trust it to come back with a better attitude.

then.text: Fog on the line today. The sheep look like wee clouds on legs.
Bit of rain never stopped a steam train. It just makes the whistle sound sadder.
Last train's back in. The engine's cooling down and so am I.

station_volunteer.text: We run a little steam train from here to the Causeway. Three kilometres, three-foot gauge, and a driver who waves at sheep.
It's a slow train. That's the point. If you wanted to arrive quickly, you wouldn't be going to the Causeway.

then.text: Headwind all the way up the coast road. I've been pedalling for an hour and I'm in the same field.
Sunshine on the North Coast! I'm going to burn and I'm going to love every second.

young_cyclist.text: {greeting} I've cycled the whole coast road to get here and I'm thrilled. My legs have asked me to stop saying thrilled.
There's a great chippy by the green. It's called the Chippy. Subtle, but it works.

post_clerk.text: Letters, parcels and gossip. Two out of three are free of charge.
I know everybody who lives here and which dog belongs to whom. It's the dogs I rely on. They're never wrong.

then.text: Right, I asked the ranger for a column back in March. For a doorstep. A man can dream. She said no, and she said it twice, in case I was thinking of a second go.
Tuesday night I had a couple from Stuttgart. They complained about my snoring at two in the morning. It's in the guest book. First time I've been grateful for it.

else.text: The Giant's Rest, bed and breakfast. Full Ulster fry, soda bread, two kinds of potato bread. Don't ask me about stones.

ct_giant_closed.text: Roped off and a path closed, and the guests ask why. I say it's the legend. They say a legend doesn't need a rope. Nobody's right.

then.text: Somebody caught Fionn mac Cumhaill, they say. I told them it was a story. It's a very good story, is it not.

else.text: The night walk's fantastic. A lantern, a story, a hot drink. And a shape in the shallows that wasn't in the brochure.

ct_giant_ferry.text: The Larne boat was twenty minutes late and nobody on it would say why. There was a very large wet footprint on the car deck, I'll tell you that.
